headline: Approved: $1.1 million for police cruisers and body cameras, and $1.5 million for 14 firefighter recruits.
summary: The meeting approved $1.1 million from free cash for police cruisers and body cameras. It approved $1.5 million to hire 14 firefighter recruits. It also approved a $180,430 PEG access fund transfer and a plan change for 278 Middlesex Street.
decisions: Approved appointments of Jennifer Gilbo to the Community Preservation Commission and Timothy Hovey to the Zoning Board of Appeals.
Approved asking the city manager to identify underused public space downtown and explore improvements.
Approved asking for information on the anticipated opening date of Bicentennial Park on Jackson Street.
Withdrawn: motion to send the $1.1 million police request to the finance subcommittee.
Approved 7-3 transfer of $1.1 million from free cash to the Lowell Police Department for cruisers and body cameras.
Approved $1.5 million supplemental appropriation for 14 new firefighter recruits; nine yes votes were read on roll call.
Referred the tree leaning toward the property at 38 Fox Street to the City Manager and DPW for report and recommendation.
Approved asking the city manager to have the proper department review the Hunts Falls Rotary on-ramp from Centerville, including signage.
Approved 8-2 asking the clerk to prepare minutes of the executive session discussion on Flock cameras for council review.
Approved asking the city manager to arrange a public Flock camera demonstration with a question and answer session.
Approved sending a letter opposing any repurposing of the ICC building into a shelter.
Approved asking the city manager for a report on the yearly cost of a property tax freeze for long-time homeowners over 75.
Referred the minimum residential factor for FY2027 to a public hearing on November 10, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Approved, with ten yes votes read on roll call, authorizing the city manager to request approval for changes to the Jam Plan for 278 Middlesex Street and surrounding parcels.
Denied motion to cut $28,430 from the $180,430 PEG transfer, reducing it to $152,000.
Approved $180,430 transfer from the PEG access fund for technology improvements and an LTC contract increase; seven yes and two no votes, with one member recused.
Four Boston Gas and National Grid utility requests (8.3 to 8.6) bundled and referred to a November 5 public hearing.
discussion: Police and fire funding: Members asked why the police and fire money was not in the budget. They discussed the free cash source and whether to send the police request to a finance subcommittee. That motion was withdrawn.

Fire overtime and hiring: Members asked whether 14 recruits would lower the $4 million overtime budget. The manager said the effect would be tested after hiring. The union said it needs more firefighters.
Flock camera review: Residents urged a public process and asked that the cameras be turned off during it. Members discussed a public demonstration and whether to release executive session minutes.
ICC building future: Members and residents discussed rumors that the building would become a shelter. A letter opposing that use was approved.
Senior tax freeze: Members discussed a property tax freeze for long-time homeowners over 75. They raised concerns about cost, eligibility rules, and other ways to help seniors.
